question.text: A thin rod having a length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and area of cross-section <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is suspended vertically from one end. The rod is cooled from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>210</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>160</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. After cooling, a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> is attached at the lower end of the rod such that the length of rod again becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Young's modulus and coefficient of linear expansion of the rod are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi></math>. (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Let Δl be the decease in length of rod due to decease in temperature

Then, Δl=lαΔT, here, coefficient of linear expansion is α=2×10-5 K-1 and ΔT=(483-433) K=50 K

Thus, Δl=1×2×10-5×50=10-3 m

Young's modulus is stated as  Y=FAΔll, here, F=Mg.

So, 2×1011=Mg×13×10-6×10-3

⇒Mg=2×1011×3×10-9=6×10-2

Thus, M=60 kg
